title: Peer block fetch: fill gaps found by gossip reconciliation
description:
Gossip reconciliation already computes a want-set (CIDs advertised by a peer that the local node does not have) but the fetch step is stubbed. The log line is: `v1: peer block fetch not yet implemented`. A new node joining the network receives tip advertisements, computes wants, and then does nothing. It stays empty indefinitely.

This is a must-have for any real deployment.

## How fetching works

The existing peering connection (NNTP over TCP) is the fetch channel. Transit peers are already connected; adding a fetch command over the existing session avoids a second connection.

Add `XCID <cid>` to the transit peering command set:
- Requester sends `XCID bafyrei...`
- Responder looks up the block in its store and replies:
  - `224 Block follows (CID)` + block bytes + `.` terminator — if found
  - `430 No such block` — if not found locally
- Requester receives bytes, verifies CID (SHA-256 of received bytes must match requested CID), runs block through `run_pipeline`

`XCID` must be advertised in the transit peering CAPABILITIES response so peers can degrade gracefully if the remote doesn't support it yet.

## Reconciliation trigger

When `handle_tip_advertisement` computes a non-empty want-set, it currently logs a warning and stops. Instead it should send want CIDs to a fetch task via an mpsc channel. The fetch task:

1. Deduplicates wants (same CID may arrive from multiple peers)
2. Picks a peer to fetch from (the peer that sent the advertisement, falling back to any connected peer)
3. Sends `XCID <cid>` over that peer's session
4. On success: runs block through `run_pipeline` (write to store, update msgid_map, append to group log, publish gossip tip)
5. On `430`: tries next available peer; after all peers exhausted, logs warning and drops the want
6. On connection error: requeues the want with backoff

## Concurrency and backpressure

- Maximum concurrent fetches: configurable (`[peering] max_concurrent_fetches`, default 8)
- Want queue bounded (drop oldest wants if queue full — tip reconciliation will re-discover them)
- Per-peer rate limiting: respect existing `PeerRateLimiter`

## Ordering concern

Blocks in the group log form a DAG (entries have `parent_cids`). Fetching a tip may require fetching parent blocks first. For v1: fetch tip blocks only; log entries with missing parents are appended with empty `parent_cids` and reconciliation re-runs on the next gossip cycle. Full DAG traversal is a follow-on.

## What does NOT need to change

- `run_pipeline` — fetched blocks go through the same path as received blocks
- Block store — fetch is a read on the remote, a write on the local; no new store operations
- Gossip topic subscription — unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- Integration test: two transit nodes, node A ingests an article, node B starts empty, B receives tip advertisement from A, B fetches and stores the article, B can serve the article via NNTP ARTICLE command
- CID verification: a block whose bytes do not hash to the requested CID is rejected with a warning and not stored
- `430` response from peer does not crash or hang the fetch task
- Fetch respects `max_concurrent_fetches` limit (test with a burst of 50 wants)
